RD REFERENCES This is UNEVALUATED Information 26 July 1955 le The city of Daugavpils (N 55-53, E 26-30) was damaged only slightly during World War II and has been largely restored, The Daugava bridge, which was being rebuilt of wood, was scheduled to be completed in the summer of 1954 25X1 Considerable building is going on in the Auburbs of Daugavpils to relieve the serious housing shortage in the city, where the population has been sharply increased by numbers of farmers who move to the city in order to avoid joining the kolkho2y.,. Many of these farmers tear down'their old houses and rebuild them with the same lumber on land granted by the city. 2. The population of Daugavpils is about half Latvian and half Russian.1 There are no longer any Germans in the city. Very few soldiers are seen on the street$. Although the general amnesty in 1953 released many criminals in the area, the latter have been in large part rearrested. 25X1 Most commodities are readily available in Daugavpils and queues are not common. Bread is hard to obtain on Wednesday and Friday of each week, when the farmers come to market and buy their supplies. Although the kolkhoz farmers have to deliver a large share of their production to the State, they are able to maintain themselves and usually keep house petq,. which supply 25X1 d f ung or their gardens. 4. The winter of 1953-1954 was very cold in eastern Latvia, the temperature measuring as low as minus 320 C. A good harvest was promised for 195ke After Stalin's death, food prices and some others decreased.
